idiom_name: axum Router::route with one async handler per page
implementation_notes: axum binds one async handler per path: Router::new().route("/orders", get(list_orders)), where the page controller is a plain async fn whose parameters are extractors (Query<PageQuery>, State<Arc<OrderService>>) and whose return type implements IntoResponse (Html<String>, Json<T>, Redirect). The classic controller object is replaced by a function plus extractor types, and shared behaviour is layered with tower middleware (Router::layer) instead of inherited. actix-web's #[get("/orders")] attribute macros are the alternative realization with the same per-page mapping; an object-per-page form is rarely justified because handlers have no state of their own - state lives in typed extractors.
pitfalls: Handlers must be Send + 'static futures: holding a non-Send value (Rc, a RefCell guard) across an await stops the router from compiling.
Extractors are consumed in order and a body-consuming extractor must come last; mixing them up turns a page handler into a compile error or a 415 at runtime.
Only one handler may own a method+path pair: registering the same route twice panics at startup unless the overlap is handled explicitly (merge/fallback).
